title: Longest Common Subpath
summary: Given a country with n cities and m friends each taking a path through these cities, find the longest common subpath shared by all friends' paths, or return 0 if no common subpath exists.
statement: Given a country with n cities and m friends each taking a path through these cities, find the longest common subpath shared by all friends' paths, or return 0 if no common subpath exists. Each path is a sequence of cities visited in order, which may include repeated cities but not consecutively.
constraints: There are at least two paths; total path length and n are at most 100000.
Cities range from 0 through n-1 and consecutive cities in a path differ.
A common subpath must be contiguous and appear in the same order in every path.
hints: If a common subpath of length L exists, every shorter prefix length is also achievable.
Double-hash every length-L window in each path and intersect the per-path hash sets.
Binary-search the greatest length with a nonempty intersection, starting from the shortest path.
Rolling hashes represent contiguous ordered windows, set intersection enforces presence in every path, and monotonicity validates the binary search.
editorial: Rolling hashes represent contiguous ordered windows, set intersection enforces presence in every path, and monotonicity validates the binary search.

tests.explanation: The paths [2,3] and [3,4] occur in all routes, but no common length-three route does.
No city occurs in every path, so the maximum common length is zero.
